title: feat: allow non-streaming text endpoints as community models
author: Drjacky

gist.summary: Community publishers can register OpenAI-compatible text endpoints that return JSON but do not support SSE. Endpoint testing records `streaming: false` and a `streamingError` when the `stream: true` probe returns JSON or a 400/422 response; SSE endpoints must still report terminal usage, while 401, 429 and 5xx responses still fail validation. Non-streaming requests use the existing proxy and usage billing. For `stream: true` requests to these models, Gen requests a JSON answer upstream and replays the completed answer as a valid Chat Completions or Responses event stream with terminal usage; streaming-by-default clients receive the whole answer at once. `/models` and `/v1/models` expose `supports_streaming: false`. The dashboard stores the test result as `advertised.streaming: false`, and `polli my-models create --no-streaming` sets the same value; the CLI is bumped to 0.1.36. The chat-stream helper was moved to `text/chat/stream.ts`, response-stream handling was generalized for completed Responses, and the bring-your-own-model and account API docs were updated.

image.prompt: In a cozy garden hackerspace, Polli and a small CRT monitor robot watch a JSON reply travel from a lime green (#ecf874) terminal into a single tidy ribbon of stream events, with code-plants blooming beside them. The main character is a cute pixel art bee mascot with a yellow body and dark brown horizontal stripes, small black legs, two black antennae, black vertical oval eyes, bright pink rectangular blush marks on cheeks, a small happy smile, and small rounded light blue translucent wings; she wears tiny headphones, stays small beside the robot, and is strictly pixel art, never realistic—cozy pixel art, 8-bit aesthetic, soft pastel gradients, warm lighting, retro gaming vibes.
